adopt:
# Source, docs and the compatibility matrix (Apache-2.0):
#   https://github.com/occupysaas/zeroauthy
git clone https://github.com/occupysaas/zeroauthy
cd zeroauthy

# Their quickstart (docs/quickstart.md) covers the TLS certificate pair and
# master.key that the server requires before it will start.
# Put cert.pem, key.pem and master.key where the run command below expects.

# Run the published image. Tag 1.0.0-rc.1 is the current public release.
docker run -d --name zeroauthy -p 8443:8443 -v zeroauthy-data:/data \
  -v "$PWD/certs:/certs:ro" \
  -e ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__LISTEN=:8443 \
  -e ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__SYSTEM_HOST=system.localhost:8443 \
  -e ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TLS_CERT_FILE=/certs/cert.pem \
  -e ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TLS_KEY_FILE=/certs/key.pem \
  -e ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__MASTER_KEY="$(cat master.key)" \
  ghcr.io/occupysaas/zeroauthy:1.0.0-rc.1

# First admin, then sign in at https://system.localhost:8443/
docker exec zeroauthy zeroauthy admin create --email you@example.com

# No Docker? Release binaries for linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and darwin/arm64
# are on their releases page, with a SHA256SUMS file.
description:
Kind: pack

What it does
Stand up zeroauthy — the Apache-2.0 Go identity provider from the OccupySaaS community — from its published container image or its release binaries. This pack installs and documents it; it never vendors or hosts it.

Runtime
